questions.question: Two boats go downstream in a river at a speed of 35 km/hr and 25 km/hr. The speed of the stream is 4 km/hr. The distance between both boats initially is 60 km. In how much time will they meet if the boats are going downstream?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When two objects move in the **same direction** (downstream), their **Relative Speed** is the difference between their individual speeds.

**Relative Speed** = 35 km/hr − 25 km/hr = 10 km/hr.

**Time** to meet = **Initial Distance** ÷ **Relative Speed**.

**Time** = 60 km ÷ 10 km/hr = 6 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed** of **Boat 1** (downstream) = 35 km/hr

**Speed** of **Boat 2** (downstream) = 25 km/hr

**Speed** of the **Stream** = 4 km/hr

**Initial Distance** between **Boats** = 60 km

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5b3b9c0bd5aaa8999eac796692fdbf2d8e43b12b1dbcd51f20227f827050516.png] 

Since both **boats** are moving in the **downstream** direction, their actual speeds over the ground are given as 35 km/hr and 25 km/hr.

⇒ **Relative Speed** = **Speed of Boat 1** − **Speed of Boat 2**

⇒ **Relative Speed** = 35 − 25 = 10 km/hr

⇒ **Time** to meet = **Distance** ÷ **Relative Speed**

⇒ **Time** = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 6 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, **Relative Speed** = S₁ − S₂ (where S₁ > S₂).

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two objects move toward each other or away from each other in opposite directions, **Relative Speed** = S₁ + S₂.

Downstream and Upstream Speed

**Downstream Speed** = Speed in Still Water + Stream Speed. **Upstream Speed** = Speed in Still Water − Stream Speed.

Time, Speed, and Distance Relation

**Time** = Distance ÷ Speed | **Distance** = Speed × Time | **Speed** = Distance ÷ Time.</p

questions.question: 25 employees can finish work in 20 days. After how many days should 10 employees leave the job so that the work is finished in 30 days?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work = 25 employees × 20 days = 500 units.

Remaining 15 employees worked for the entire 30 days = 15 × 30 = 450 units.

Deficit work = 500 − 450 = 50 units.

This deficit was completed by the 10 employees who left later.

Number of days they worked = 50 units ÷ 10 employees = 5 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **employees** (M₁) = 25

Initial **days** (D₁) = 20

Total **duration** to finish work = 30 days

Employees who **left** = 10

**Formula:**

Total Work = M × D

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9461cc74296f0bc6ea24f59285306a5aaa42c9ce00a2be749e8c170a9bc2daa8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Work** = 25 × 20 = 500 units

⇒ Let 10 employees leave after **x days**.

⇒ Work done by 25 employees in **x days** = 25 × x = 25x

⇒ Remaining employees = 25 − 10 = 15

⇒ Remaining days = 30 − x

⇒ Work done by 15 employees in **(30 − x) days** = 15(30 − x)

⇒ 25x + 15(30 − x) = 500

⇒ 25x + 450 − 15x = 500

⇒ 10x = 500 − 450

⇒ 10x = 50

⇒ x = 5 days

**∴ The correct answer is 5 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

The M-D-H Formula

Work is proportional to workers, days, and hours: (M₁D₁H₁)/W₁ = (M₂D₂H₂)/W₂.

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work (E ∝ 1/T).

Remaining Work Concept

In cases of leaving/joining, Total Work = (Work done before change) + (Work done after change).</p

questions.question: If the curved surface area of a solid cylinder is two-fifths of its total surface area, then what is the ratio of its diameter to its height?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** to **Total Surface Area (TSA)** is 2 : 5.

In a cylinder, CSA / TSA = h / (r + h).

⇒ h / (r + h) = 2 / 5

⇒ If **height (h)** = 2 units, then **radius (r)** = 5 − 2 = 3 units.

⇒ **Diameter (d)** = 2 × r = 2 × 3 = 6 units.

⇒ Ratio of **Diameter** to **Height** = 6 : 2 = 3 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2/5 × Total Surface Area (TSA)

**Formula Used:**

⇒ CSA of cylinder = 2πrh

⇒ TSA of cylinder = 2πr(r + h)

⇒ Diameter (d) = 2r

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97bf67c146341cd924da3f24fe3e9fd311df97d8decefbb12080af7903cee0a5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2πrh = (2/5) × 2πr(r + h)

⇒ h = (2/5) × (r + h)

⇒ 5h = 2(r + h)

⇒ 5h = 2r + 2h

⇒ 5h − 2h = 2r

⇒ 3h = 2r

Since **Diameter (d)** = 2r:

⇒ 3h = d

⇒ d / h = 3 / 1

⇒ d : h = 3 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cylinder

The amount of space occupied by the cylinder is given by V = πr²h.

Base Area of a Cylinder

The area of each circular face of the cylinder is A = πr².

Surface Area Relationship

The **Total Surface Area** is the sum of the **Curved Surface Area** and the areas of the two circular bases: TSA = CSA + 2 × Base Area.</p

__
 
• The lowermost layer of the atmosphere with an average height of 13 km (16 km over the equator and 6 km over the poles).
 
• The air we breathe exists here. Almost all the weather phenomena (like rainfall, fog, clouds, dew, frost and hailstorm) occur in this layer.
 
• Temperature decreases with increasing height at the rate of 6.5℃ per 1000m. This is called normal lapse rate.
 
• The height of the troposphere varies from the equator towards the pole (decreases towards the poles) and from one season to another (increases during summer while decreases during winter) during a year.
 
• The upper limit is called the tropopause which is 1.5 km thick. (The word “troposphere” literally means “zone/region of mixing” and tropopause menas “where the mixing stops”.)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Stratosphere

 
• Above the troposphere lies the stratosphere. It extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• This layer is almost free from clouds and associated weather phenomena, making conditions most ideal for flying aeroplanes.
 
• One important feature of the stratosphere is that it contains a layer of ozone gas between the height of 15 to 30 km (also called Ozonosphere).
 
• Temperature increases with height due to the absorption of UV rays by the ozone layer.
 
• The upper limit of the stratosphere is known as stratopause.

Mesosphere

 
• Lying above the stratosphere this is the third layer of the atmosphere and extends between 50 km and 80 km.
 
• Meteorites burn up in this layer on entering from space.
 
• Temperature decreases with increasing height again.
 
• The uppermost limit is the mesopause where the temperature becomes -80℃.

Ozone Layer

 
• The ozone layer is an area or a continuous region in the stratosphere of the earth that includes high concentrations of ozone(O₃) and protects the earth from the sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

Thermosphere

 
• Temperature here rises very rapidly with increasing height.
 
• The International Space Station is situated in this layer.
 
• It is further divided into two layers:

Ionosphere:

 
• It extends between 80 - 400 km.
 
• This layer helps in radio transmission. In fact, radio waves transmitted from the earth are reflected back to the earth by this layer.
 
• Includes a number of ionic layers with increasing heights like the D layer, E layer, F layer and G layer.
